scope_review: The learner drives or prepares a normal passenger car; no specialist vehicle operating rules.
learning_objective: Distinguish braking-distance growth from speed growth
novelty_review: Different from reaction-time calculation and legal speed limits: tests the approximate square relationship of braking distance to speed at unchanged grip and braking conditions.
scenario: Natural roadside photograph on a closed driver-training track in France: one ordinary grey passenger car in three-quarter front view on a broad straight dry tarmac surface, with a few orange cones far off its path and empty run-off area. fr.question_text: À adhérence et conditions de freinage identiques, si la vitesse double, la distance de freinage est approximativement :
fr.explanation: Dans les mêmes conditions, la distance de freinage augmente approximativement avec le carré de la vitesse : doubler la vitesse la multiplie donc par quatre. Cela concerne le freinage, pas à lui seul toute la distance d’arrêt.

en.question_text: With the same grip and braking conditions, if speed doubles, the braking distance is approximately:
en.explanation: Under the same conditions, braking distance increases approximately with the square of speed, so doubling speed multiplies it by four. This describes braking distance, not the whole stopping distance on its own.

visual_review: Reviewed ordinary passenger car on dry training track, cones away from vehicle path, no skid or racing situation. Question explicitly holds grip and braking conditions constant; D follows d=k*v^2, so d(2v)=4d(v). Both languages qualify approximation and distinguish braking from stopping distance.
